chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Gary Anderson's advice on recording Road Father: start with Fire Dance
summary: Herman recalls Anderson's advice to start the album with the hardest piece, Fire Dance, because if they got past it the rest would follow.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: But did you ever think of -- from this aspect, did you think of it, like, imagine what we could do if we really prepared an album to be that we'd done, with all the help you can get, and doing it well, instead of just doing it and saying, 'Well, we have to get through this.'
Uh-huh, I see what you're saying.

In other words, if you think about the psychology which was given to me by -- really, the whole philosophy and psychology (unintelligible) of the 'Road Father' simply by the album was given to me by Gary Anderson. He said, 'Let's start with the Fire Dance.' And I said, 'Start with Fire Dance?' Because if we get beyond that, we'll be able to do that whole side of the album.
And if we blow that one, we're out of business, anyway.
Let's get it over in one fell swoop. And I appreciate that kind of advice.
